title: Disclose AI in text on X, LinkedIn
statement: On X and LinkedIn, which have no reliable per-post AI switch, state provenance in the post text (e.g. '3D animation rendered in code', 'AI-assisted illustrations, demo figures'), match the video's fine print, and never strip or forge provenance metadata.
evidence: Pack rule filling a platform gap (no per-post switch at the time of writing).

sources.locator: AI-content disclosure: X and LinkedIn; File metadata

notes: Generated people also get a line in the end-card fine print (story-script, Honesty inside the story).

title: Instagram AI label always on
statement: Switch Instagram's AI label on for every video the pipeline makes and confirm the switch reads on before Share, because it defaults off.
evidence: Platform spec asks for labels on photoreal or realistic altered media; switching it on for all pipeline output is a pack rule.

sources.locator: AI-content disclosure: what each switch means

notes: Inferred, not proven: accounts that auto-posted hundreds of videos got an account-level AI badge and very low reach; the posting pattern is the likely cause, not honest per-post labels.

title: TikTok AI setting on when generated
statement: Set TikTok's AI-generated content option on whenever generated imagery, voices or photoreal renders appear, and on when unsure.
evidence: Platform spec requires labels on realistic AI content and may label from content credentials; the 'when unsure, on' default is a pack rule.

sources.locator: AI-content disclosure: what each switch means

title: YouTube synthetic label: photoreal only
statement: Answer YouTube's altered-or-synthetic question Yes when any shot is photoreal generated or rendered content that could pass as real (a product that does not exist yet, a generated person, a realistic scene) and No for stylised CG, animation and motion graphics.
evidence: Platform spec (realistic content needs disclosure, animation is exempt, the label does not limit reach) applied as a pack rule.

sources.locator: AI-content disclosure: what each switch means

title: Fit length to the platform
statement: Organic shorts run 15-35 s, ads 15-30 s plus a 6 s bumper, X 20-45 s, LinkedIn 30-60 s and web heroes 20-45 s.
evidence: house preset table; the 15-35 s Shorts ideal is listed as an unverified number in the virality evidence notes.
notes: Launch films override this: L1 1:30-2:30, L9 1:45-3:00.

title: LinkedIn: H.264 MP4, aim 30-60 s
statement: LinkedIn takes 16:9, 1:1 or 4:5 (aspect 1:2.4 to 2.4:1) as MP4 with H.264 and AAC, 3 s to 15 min, aim 30-60 s organic and 15-30 s for ads.
evidence: Platform spec for the ad aim and limits; the organic aim is a pack default.

title: Master 16:9, re-layout never crop
statement: Master the launch post at 16:9 and make 9:16 and 1:1 by re-layout, never by crop or letterbox, plus a 6 s cut-down.
evidence: launch study: every film in one 2026 launch wave was 16:9 on X; re-layout is a house rule.
notes: eyes/composition catches unrequested bars (visual.no_letterbox_vertical) but not a crop, and nothing checks which aspect leads. | eyes/composition flags unrequested bars and wrong aspect; 9:16 film looks are re-laid out, never letterboxed.

title: Upload video natively to X
statement: Upload launch and feature videos natively to X; use a YouTube link only for long-form episodes.
evidence: every reference launch video (17 posts) was a native X upload; YouTube links appeared only for long-form interviews on 2 accounts.

title: Reels and TikTok: 9:16, 15-35 s
statement: Instagram Reels and TikTok take 9:16 at 1080x1920, aim 15-35 s; Reels run up to 180 s, and TikTok publishes no ideal length and shows each account's limit at upload.
evidence: Reels 180 s from press reports of a platform change; the aim is a pack default.
notes: references/platforms.md tags Reels up to 3 min as [pub]; patterns/lengths.json grades it practitioner because the help page did not render.

title: Re-layout each aspect, never crop
statement: Author the lead aspect natively and generate 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1 from per-aspect layout constants (positions, sizes, camera distance, lens shift), never by cropping or hand-editing the derived file, then check stills from each delivered file.
evidence: pack re-layout rule; eyes fails a delivered file whose aspect the platform does not take.

sources.locator: What the market sells; comparison row 'Aspect versions'

The aspect check does not prove the layout was re-authored. | Merged: Make every aspect from one timeline by re-layout: vertical gets bigger type and fewer elements, square gets tighter holds, wide gets more spatial context. title: Cut short skits to 12-15 s
statement: Cut chat-skits and story shorts for Shorts to 12-15 s.
evidence: team rule from own Shorts: every top Short lost half its viewers between 4 and 8 s and 83% swiped away; the 12-15 s value was not A/B tested.

sources.locator: YouTube, last 28 days; How to apply

notes: Disagrees with patterns/lengths.json youtube.shorts aim_s [15, 35] (house) and skills/story-script/SKILL.md chat-skit 10-40 s; this rule is narrower and evidence-led for skits on a small channel.

title: Shorts: 9:16, aim 15-35 s
statement: YouTube Shorts take 9:16 at 1080x1920, up to 180 s, aim 15-35 s; a Short over 60 s with a copyright claim on its music is blocked.
evidence: Platform spec for the 180 s limit and the 60 s copyright block (help page accessed 2026-10-16); the 15-35 s aim is a pack default.
notes: mp.check.size enforces WxH against the aspect; length is not checked. Replays count as views since 31 Mar 2025.

title: Wide 5% title-safe, square 6/10%
statement: In 16:9 keep text inside 5% title-safe (96 px sides, 54 px top and bottom at 1920x1080; 3.5% action-safe), and in 1:1 inside top 6%, bottom 10%, sides 6%.
evidence: broadcast title-safe convention for 16:9; the square row is the pack's platform preset estimate.
notes: 16:9 grid: 12 columns, 96 px margins, 24 px gutters; 1:1 grid 6 columns.

title: Landscape is fine on X
statement: On X a 16:9 master is fine: deliver landscape unless the format is a square loop.
evidence: 8 of 9 tier-A video references on X across rounds 7-8 are landscape (one about 1.72:1); one small-sample square loop; the tier-A* launch hero is 16:9.
notes: mp.check.size only checks WxH against the planned aspect, not the choice.

title: Name by 1 s or at the end
statement: On X the brand name shows by 1 s, or is held back to the end card; both shapes appear in tier-A films.
evidence: Two tier-A round-7 films name the product by 1 s; a third holds it to the end card (35.6 s of 37.8 s); a tier-A founder film (round 8) shows no logo until the last 2 s.

title: X: 20-45 s, 140 s cap
statement: X takes 9:16 or 16:9 (16:9 for cinematic pieces), aim 20-45 s; accounts without a paid tier cap a video at 140 s and 512 MB.
evidence: Platform limit read from a search summary of the help page (fetch blocked); the aim is a pack default.
notes: patterns/lengths.json grades the 140 s limit practitioner; references/platforms.md tags it [pub].
